title: Scope native CycloneDX SBOM dogfood support
description: Investigate the Spring PetClinic testClasses dogfood blocker where :cyclonedxBom and :cyclonedxDirectBom declare SBOM outputs and currently fail closed. If promoted, strict Rust dogfood must pass spring-petclinic-testclasses with no JVM task forwards, task/output/hash parity, and existing supported/external/unsupported gates must remain green. If not promoted, PARITY/dogfood/Beads must document exact missing SBOM contract pieces and the fail-closed diagnostic must remain precise.
notes: CycloneDX investigation evidence: Spring PetClinic clean testClasses upstream executes :cyclonedxDirectBom and :cyclonedxBom and writes build/reports/cyclonedx-direct/bom.json, bom.xml, build/reports/cyclonedx/application.cdx.json, plus copied build/resources/main/META-INF/sbom/application.cdx.json. The captured Rust task contract for CyclonedxDirectTask contains 166 path inputs and two outputs but only generic values (action_count/enabled/source/taskName/taskType); it does not contain Gradle resolved dependency edge graph, component metadata/properties, scope mapping, CycloneDX plugin options, serial/timestamp policy, or XML/JSON generation semantics. CyclonedxAggregateTask only captures the two direct BOM files as inputs and one output. Direct and aggregate JSON differ in serialNumber, timestamp, metadata.component.type, and many dependency orderings. Conclusion: native promotion would be fake/unsafe with the current contract. Keep fail-closed and add a follow-up for a schema-backed native SBOM contract if we want to promote this dogfood slice.
close_reason: Scoped CycloneDX dogfood promotion and documented why it must remain fail-closed with the current contract. Evidence captured: upstream task list, declared SBOM outputs and hashes, captured task contracts, missing semantic fields, and direct-vs-aggregate JSON differences. Follow-up gradle-fork-9vg6 tracks the real schema-backed SBOM IR needed before native promotion.

title: Epic: Production Readiness — Authoritative Mode + Real Execution
description:
The scaffold is complete (33 services, 560 Rust tests, 27 shadow adapters, 261 Java tests). This epic covers the remaining work to make Gradle actually run builds through Rust.

## Strategy
Rather than replacing Gradle's subsystems wholesale (which would take years), we take an incremental approach:
1. Cut over already-validated subsystems to authoritative mode
2. Enhance Rust services to handle real workloads
3. Add Rust-native task execution for simple task types
4. Gather differential testing data from real builds

## Execution Order
- Wave 1 (safety): Authoritative cut-over + differential testing
- Wave 2 (enhancement): Dependency resolution, toolchain, incremental compilation
- Wave 3 (execution): Rust-native task execution for simple tasks
- Wave 4 (optimization): Parallel execution, caching, build caching

title: Design native CycloneDX SBOM contract before promotion

Task graph lowering maps CyclonedxDirectTask/CyclonedxAggregateTask to CycloneDxSbom only when sbom_contract_json_b64 is present; real captured tasks without the IR still do not lower. title: Rust-native Java compilation via javac process
description:
Implement Java compilation task execution in Rust by spawning javac as a child process.

## What to do
1. Create JavaCompileExecutor that:

We don't need to reimplement javac in Rust. We just need to ORCHESTRATE the javac process

Rust can manage the javac process lifecycle, parallel compilation of modules,
and classpath construction without JVM overhead.
